steps.text: Combine ground beef and onion in a large saucepan over medium heat; stir until meat is brown and onion is tender, 5 to 7 minutes.

Stir in tomato sauce, kidney beans, and stewed tomatoes. For a thinner consistency, add water. Add chili powder, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover and let simmer, about 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Homemade Chili
raw_recipe.description: This easy homemade chili recipe made with ground beef, onion, tomatoes, beans, and seasonings cooks in just 20 minutes for a crowd-pleasing meal.

video.description: In this video, learn how to make easy homemade chili with the Allrecipes team. Boiled and simmered to perfection, this beloved Tex Mex dinner dish combines tender ground beef with juicy tomatoes and protein-packed kidney beans for a well-rounded (and affordable) meal.
video.name: How to Make Easy Homemade Chili

review.reviewBody: This is the quickest thing I have made for dinner in a long time. However, I like my chili on the thicker side, and this chili was a little too watery. To solve this problem, I added half a can of tomato paste, and this made it perfect. I also added just a little extra chili powder because I wanted it to be a little spicier. Because I didn't have stewed tomatoes, I used canned diced tomatoes instead. They were just as good and gave the chili a nice flavor. I have already made this for dinner twice, and I plan on making it a staple in my recipe collection. It's great served with a portion of baguette.

I decided to make chili dogs at the last minute for National Hot Dog Day, I needed something fast. This fit the bill perfectly. I increased the chili powder and garlic powder and added a few more spices (cumin, mexican oregano, crushed red pepper, onion powder, little brown sugar, little Worchestershire sauce) for flavor. This worked out great.

Absolutely fantastic. I make the following modifications to the 1x recipe: add two onions instead of one, each cut into 6 wedges, and add a 16 oz box of sliced baby bella mushrooms with the onions in Step 1. Add a full teaspoon of garlic powder, salt and pepper. Also I don't add any water.

Great quick and easy recipe. I doubled the chilli powder, added a tsp each of cumin, onion powder, turmeric and a dash of worchestershire for added flavour. Also used fresh garlic and celery that I added to the pan with the meat and onions. I opted for red kidney and white beans. Great on dogs with melted cheese or in a bowl with a good crusty bread.

Good starter recipe. I made it 4x, added (1) green pepper, (1) red pepper, (4) jalapenos, (8) garlic cloves from jar, bottle of beer instead of water, (2) teaspoon cumin, (2) teaspoons cayenne red pepper flakes.

It was ok although much too soupy and very bland, I added a lot of extra garlic powder, chili powder, and salt. I also recommend that you season the meat and onion with the garlic and chili powders then add the other ingredients.

Use a potato masher to really "dechunk" the meat.I add a shot of sourmash,sauté bell pepper & celery with the onion and add frozen yellow corn just before simmering the chili for about two hr.Adding pinto beans helps thicken. Do not over cook the onion& vegetables.One T. of olive oil helps them sauté mor evenly.
added a couple celery stalks chopped small and some red and orange sweet peppers, red and pinto beans…now to plate with some elbow macaroni, cheddar cheese and a dollop of sour cream!

I doubled the recipe. It made a lot more than I meant to, so I hope it freezes good. LOL Anyway, It's really DELICIOUS originally as written here. I didn't use the beans, though (I don't really like chili with beans). I DID add a few things, though, just to experiment and stretch it a little. Yes, it stretched it a bit more than intended. 😅 I diced 1 large potato into it, minced one deseeded large jalapeno pepper, 6 small carrots, peeled and sliced to about ½", 1 tsp smoked paprika and about ½ tsp fresh cilantro... Waiting for it to boil and thicken to see how it turns out. I may need to add some flour or corn starch to thicken it, cause I didn't drain the tomatoes . Smells and tastes good so far. Yeah, I dunno what's up with the potato. For some reason people in this part of Texas want potato and sometimes carrots in their chili? If anyone tries my lil experimental ingredients, remember I made it for a double recipe so you don't overpower the flavor with paprika and cilantro.

Made this recipe tonight for the family. I started with the onion and cooked it in bacon grease before adding the ground beef. When seasoning I topped it with Cajun two step seasoning(it has a soft kick but has a sweet taste to it) and it is a total game changer, highly recommend

Absolute best chili recipe (Fast cook so you’re not overcooking your ingredients). For a hardier chili you can omit the water or broth. In this recipe I also add paprika, Italian seasoning, cloves, allspice, and fresh chopped garlic (towards the end of cooking) (all the spices can be added while browning the meat to bring out the fragrance of the spice). For a nice change up, swap out the ground beef using ground lamb. Bon appétit.

I made it and added 1/2 teaspoons chili powder. Also 1/2 teaspoon of brown sugar. Let it simmer for 45 minutes after it came to a boil. Might add green peppers to it next time. It was good with rice. Also tried it with Fritos. Definitely recommend.
I enjoyed this recipe! I plan to use it often during cold days especially when I have to do a quick dinner. Love using the crock pot with this recipe.
This was an amazing chili, I added chopped jalapeño and banana peppers to give it a bit of heat but this is a favorite in my house. Thank you for the simple and delicious recipe!
No changes it's great
Great, just swap the beef for veggie ground- same taste/no plaque!
Churched this up a bit with habanero peppers.
I added cummin, pinto beans, and little flakes of red pepper! DELICIOUS thank you
This is an easy recipe to following and it allows me to add any veggies to make cleaning eating feel more healthier
I added a couple of shakes of red pepper flakes, Cayenne pepper. About a teaspoon of tomato paste and I thickened it with a slurry of flour and water.
